hero.h1: Trenchless Sewer Repair in McHenry, IL
hero.sub: A sewer line that needs replacing doesn't have to mean a trench through your lawn. We line or replace the pipe through small openings after a camera shows exactly what's wrong. From our office on West Elm Street, serving McHenry County.

img.alt: Two J. Blanton plumbers pouring resin into a sewer liner bag to prepare a trenchless pipe lining

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Trenchless sewer repair, also called no-dig sewer repair, fixes a damaged pipe without digging a trench along its full length. Instead of opening up your yard from the house to the street, we work through one or two access points and repair the pipe from the inside or replace it in place. There are two main methods: cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining and pipe bursting. Both fix the line underground, so what's above it stays untouched.

img.alt: Two J. Blanton plumbers setting up sewer camera and cable equipment beside a home's foundation before a trenchless sewer repair

blocks.intro: Trenchless repair makes the most sense in McHenry when digging would be messy, deep or wet.

items.h3: Wet Ground Near the River and Lakes
items.body: High groundwater near the Fox River and the Chain O'Lakes can turn an open trench into a pumping job. Lining avoids most of that.
Many homes have patios, landscaping and long driveways over the sewer path. Small access points leave them in place.
When roots or age have opened joints along the whole line, a liner seals every one of them at once.
A liner follows the pipe, so a real sag is fixed with a small spot dig first. We'll tell you if that's your situation.

blocks.h2: Trenchless Sewer Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Can a liner fix a sagging sewer line?
items.preview: No. It follows the sag. The low spot needs a spot repair.
items.answer: No. A liner takes the shape of the pipe it's in, so a sag stays a sag. We fix the low section with a small dig, and the rest can be lined if needed.

items.q: How long does a sewer liner last?
items.answer: Liners are designed to last for decades. Once cured, there are no joints for roots or groundwater to get through.

items.q: Will a trenchless repair disturb my lawn?
items.preview: Very little. Usually one or two small openings.
items.answer: Very little. Most jobs need one or two small access points instead of a trench the length of the line.
Many residential jobs are done in a day or two, depending on length and prep.

items.q: How much does trenchless sewer repair cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on length, depth and method. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on how much of the line needs work, the depth, the method and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
